Why we moved our queue to Postgres

For three years our background jobs ran on a dedicated message broker. It worked, but every incident review ended with the same question: why does a system with one database need a second stateful service just to remember which jobs are left?

What we tried

We replaced the broker with a jobs table and SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Workers claim a batch, process it and delete the rows in the same transaction, so a crash simply releases the lock and another worker picks the job up.

  • One fewer service to deploy, monitor and back up.
  • Jobs are enqueued in the same transaction as the data they refer to.

Throughput stayed well above what we need, and the on-call rotation got noticeably quieter.
